name: Joeka-Oajana Pidgin
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: de Goeje, C. H. 1908. Bijlage II A: De 'handelstaal' der Joeka's met de Trio's en Ojana's. In Verslag der Toemoekhoemak-expeditie, pp. 204-219. Leiden: Brill.
sources.note: Transcription key p. 204: 'accent, indien niet aangegeven, op voorlaatste lettergreep' (accent, where not marked, on the penultimate syllable) -- a wordlist convention for the NDYUKA-lexified trade language used with Trio and Wayana (Glottolog ndyu1241, 'Joeka-Trio' in hh.bib), not for the Wayana/Carib-lexified pidgin Glottolog files as joek1234.

sources.citation: Crevaux, Jules. 1883. Voyages dans l'Amerique du Sud. Paris: Hachette.
sources.note: Travel narrative containing ~25 further pidgin phrases; grep for accent/prononc finds no remark on the accentuation of 'roucouyenne' words (only a note that 'agouti' is pronounced as in French).

sources.citation: Bakker, Peter, Tobias Gretenkort & Mikael Parkvall. 2018. Dr. Crevaux's Wayana-Carib Pidgin of the Guyanas: a grammatical sketch. Amerindia 40: 169-217.
sources.note: Section 4.7 Phonology (pp. 213-214) covers only vowel/consonant inventory, diphthongs, clusters and CV syllable shape, based on Crevaux's written notes; nothing on stress or accent. p. 212: 'We can assume that intonation plays some role in distinguishing between questions and statements, but there is no evidence for this in the text.' p. 214: 'There is no indication of length, nasality, glottalization, etc. for any of the vowels.' Silent on word stress.

sources.citation: de Goeje, C. H. 1906. Bijdrage tot de ethnographie der Surinaamsche Indianen. Internationales Archiv fuer Ethnographie XVII, Supplement. Leiden: Brill.
sources.note: Key pp. 34-35 (for the expedition's Indian languages generally): stress is marked, 'Wanneer de Indiaan een woord afzonderlijk opgeeft, legt hij den klemtoon dikwijls anders dan wanneer hij datzelfde woord in een gesprek gebruikt. De waarnemingen omtrent klemtoon zijn dientengevolge onvolledig en het zou voorbarig zijn een vaste regel op te stellen.' pp. 109-111 'Handelsdialekt tusschen Aucaners en Indianen' wordlist (Ndyuka-lexified), no stress rule.

sources.citation: Adam, Lucien. 1882. Grammaire de la langue roucouyenne. In Crevaux, Sagot & Adam 1882 (BLA VIII), pp. 21-31.
sources.note: Comparative morphosyntactic notice (pronouns, verb, tense, word order, Galibi affinities); already notes the material is a 'baragouin de traite'; no section on sounds and no mention of accent/stress.

sources.citation: Crevaux, Jules. 1882. Vocabulaire Francais-Roucouyenne. In Crevaux, Sagot & Adam, Grammaires et vocabulaires Roucouyenne, Arrouague, Piapoco et d'autres langues de la region des Guyanes (Bibliotheque Linguistique Americaine VIII), pp. 1-20. Paris: Maisonneuve.
sources.note: Plain French-Roucouyenne wordlist with example phrases; no preface on pronunciation, no explanation of the acute accents (French orthographic <e>), nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Meira, Sergio & Pieter Muysken. 2017. Cariban in contact: New perspectives on Trio-Ndyuka pidgin. In Kofi Yakpo & Pieter Muysken (eds.), Boundaries and Bridges: Language Contact in Multilingual Ecologies, 197-228. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.note: Per Bakker et al. 2018 (pp. 182-185), p. 119 of this chapter discusses the Wayana jargon/'simplified Wayana' of de Goeje and compares its vocabulary with Wayana, Trio and Kalinha; it is the only modern sketch with a phonology of the sibling Ndyuka-Trio pidgin and may say something about accent in the trade languages of the region. Not opened (paywalled; Google Books preview blocked).
